To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The Turkish health care system has a strong focus on the medicalization of smoking cessation, with the use of nicotine replacement therapy and pharmaceuticals; and 2) nurses are in a unique position to engage with smokers and help them quit, but they need to receive training to deliver cessation advice and to be incentivized for their efforts.

nurses are important providers of smoking cessation advice in Turkey, but that there are challenges to their involvement.

the training of health care providers, particularly nurses, in smoking cessation as an integral part of patient care.
the training of nurses and the role of the health system in supporting cessation in Turkey.

the development of a culturally sensitive cessation training program for nurses in Turkey, a country that is experiencing a rapid increase in smoking rates and where there is no routine cessation counseling for patients.

the nurses and doctors need to be trained both on the systemic harms of tobacco use and cessation counseling skills.

nurses can be a powerful force for change in smoking cessation, but they require training and support.
the nurses in Turkey have a very important role to play in the prevention of smoking.
nurses are the most appropriate health professionals to provide smoking cessation counseling.

the health system in Turkey needs to be reformed to make smoking cessation a priority for all health care providers.
